newsitem.title: UK: Berisford slips after profits warning.
newsitem.headline: Berisford slips after profits warning.

text.p: Shares in Berisford International Plc fell on Monday after the UK food service equipment, building and consumer products group quantified the impact on profits of strike action and a downturn in demand at its Welbit unit in the U.S., traders said.
The company said it now expected year profits before tax and exceptional items would be not less than 25 million stg.
Berisford reported profits of 26.9 million stg in 1995.
The shares were down 23p at 123-1/2p in early trading, a drop of over 15 percent.

Berisford said the impact of the strike at its Darlington plant in north-east England will cost it around 3.5 million stg and a downturn in demand at its Welbit unit in the U.S. would also hit profits.
"Most analysts had been looking for profits above 33 million stg. The main shock in the statement is the general level of demand that seems to have hit Welbit," said an analyst.

Business disruption and additional charges at Welbit's Cleveland subsidiary associated with difficulties arising from the introduction in July of a new computer system would hit profits by a further 2.6 million stg, the company said.
The company added that it expected to propose a final dividend of 3.0 pence to make a total dividend of 4.5p compared to 3.0 pence in 1995.
